history.period: Ganga era origins (possibly as early as the 2nd century per Wikipedia - weakly sourced); Chola epigraphs from Rajaraja's reign and 1012 AD, mandapa by Rajendra Chola I c. 1030 AD; renovated by Vijayanagara kings in the 15th century
history.summary: Kolaramma is the presiding goddess of Kolar town; the temple in the Fort Area is over a thousand years old. Under the Gangas the deity was worshipped as Pidariyar Chamundeswary of the Saptha Matrikas, the Gangas' principal goddess; the Cholas reconstructed the temple (epigraphs of Rajaraja, 1012 AD; mandapa built by Rajendra Chola I c. 1030 AD) and the Vijayanagara kings renovated it in the 15th century. The L-shaped granite temple has two sanctums sharing a common mukha mantapa - Kolaramma (seen by devotees through a grid of mirrors) and the Sapta Matrikas, with shrines to Chellaramma (the scorpion goddess, believed to guard against scorpion stings), Ganesha and Veerabhadra; 30+ inscriptions in Tamil and Kannada survive. The Mysore royal family is said to have visited for the goddess's blessings. A floor hundi (offering well) tradition - coins dropped into a deep pit, audible for hundreds of years - continues.

name: Kolaramma Temple
town_description: Kolar, about 70 km east of Bengaluru, is one of Karnataka's oldest cities - known in antiquity as Kolahala, Kuvalala and Kolala, and once the capital of the Western Gangas. Nicknamed the 'Golden Land of India' for the historic Kolar Gold Fields nearby, it is a temple town whose landmarks include the Kolaramma and Someshwara temples, Antaragange hill, and the Avani temple cluster.
